title: A Hiss to Help the Sleeping Brain
paragraphs: Brief bursts of pink noise, a low-pitched hiss, played during sleep might give people with early-stage Alzheimer's disease a slight memory boost, according to a small study of 37 participants who had been diagnosed with the disease and had mild cognitive impairment affecting memory. There is some evidence that exposure to pink noise during sleep may help clear waste products from the brain, and the researchers reasoned that it could also support the consolidation of memories, a process that Alzheimer's can disrupt and that relies on slow brainwaves and short bursts of neural activity.

On two evenings fourteen days apart, the volunteers came to the laboratory, memorised 30 word pairs and slept there while their brain activity was monitored. On the first night, a system designed by a Spanish neurotechnology company detected when slow brainwaves were about to peak and triggered a 50-millisecond pulse of pink noise each time; on the second night no noise was played. The timing matters, according to team member Javier Minguez, because the useful window is only about 200 milliseconds wide. After each night the participants tried to recall the pairs, and they remembered 0.88 more pairs, on average, after the night with pink noise, which the researchers equate to an improvement of about 19 per cent. They stress, however, that the clinical significance remains uncertain, and they disclose that several authors have commercial links to the company or its spin-off and that three are inventors on a pending patent covering the method.

spans.contextSentence: On the first night, a system designed by a Spanish neurotechnology company detected when slow brainwaves were about to peak and triggered a 50-millisecond pulse of pink noise each time; on the second night no noise was played.
spans.contextSentenceTr: İlk gece, bir İspanyol nöroteknoloji şirketinin tasarladığı bir sistem yavaş beyin dalgalarının ne zaman zirve yapmak üzere olduğunu algıladı ve her seferinde 50 milisaniyelik bir pembe gürültü darbesi başlattı; ikinci gece hiç gürültü çalınmadı.

spans.contextSentence: After each night the participants tried to recall the pairs, and they remembered 0.88 more pairs, on average, after the night with pink noise, which the researchers equate to an improvement of about 19 per cent.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Pink noise has improved memory in people with Alzheimer's, which means that it clears waste products from their brains during sleep.
options.explanation: Atık temizliği yalnızca 'bazı kanıt' olarak anılan arka plandır; bellek artışının nedeninin bu olduğu gösterilmemiştir.

options.text: Pink noise timed to brainwaves improved recall slightly in early Alzheimer's, which means the gain is small and of unclear importance.
options.explanation: Yavaş dalgaların zirvesine göre zamanlanan gürültü 0,88 çiftlik bir artış sağladı; araştırmacılar klinik önemi belirsiz bulur.

options.text: Pink noise has improved recall in a large trial, which means that its benefit holds for healthy older adults as well as patients.
options.explanation: Çalışma 37 katılımcılı küçük bir çalışmadır ve yalnızca hafif bilişsel bozukluğu olan Alzheimer hastalarında yapılmıştır.

options.text: Pink noise improved recall on the night it was played, which means that continuous exposure works as well as timed pulses would.
options.explanation: Gürültü 50 milisaniyelik kısa darbelerle, yavaş dalga zirvesine göre verilir; zamanlamanın kritik olduğu vurgulanır.

questions.prompt: Why does the timing of each pulse matter, according to Minguez?

options.text: Longer pulses would wake the sleeping participants and spoil the experiment.
options.explanation: Uyanma riskinden söz edilmez; darbe 50 milisaniyedir.

options.text: The noise can only help during a very brief period of about a fifth of a second.
options.explanation: Minguez zamanlamanın kritik olduğunu çünkü yararlı aralığın yaklaşık 200 milisaniye olduğunu söyler.

options.text: The system can only detect slow brainwaves when they are at their lowest point.
options.explanation: Sistem yavaş dalgaların zirveye yaklaştığını saptar.

options.text: Participants could not memorise the word pairs until the noise had stopped.
options.explanation: Kelime çiftleri akşam, uykudan önce ezberlendi; gürültüyle ilgisi yoktur.

questions.prompt: In the first paragraph, 'reasoned' is closest in meaning to

options.text: argued on the basis of existing evidence
options.explanation: 'Reasoned' mevcut kanıttan yola çıkarak akıl yürütmek demektir; metin bunun henüz kanıtlanmadığını, yalnızca makul bir gerekçe olduğunu belirtir.
Önceki deneylerde gösterildiği söylenmez; bu, olasılığı sınayan küçük bir çalışmadır.
Araştırmacılar şüphe duymaz; bellek pekiştirmesine katkıyı makul bulur.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the final sentences of the passage?

options.text: The company's method has proved effective enough to be offered to hospitals straight away, as the data stand.
options.explanation: Araştırmacılar klinik anlamlılığın belirsiz olduğunu söyler ve patent beklemededir; hastanelerde hemen kullanılabileceği söylenmez.

options.text: The pending patent is likely to stop other research teams from repeating the experiment themselves.
options.explanation: Patentin başka grupların çalışmayı tekrarlamasını engellediği söylenmez; metin yalnızca bazı yazarların buluş sahibi olduğunu bildirir.

options.text: The reported gain is of uncertain importance, and the authors' ties to the company call for care.
options.explanation: Yazarlar klinik önemi belirsiz bulur ve ticari bağlantılarını açıklar; bu, sonuca temkinli yaklaşmak için iki ayrı gerekçedir.

options.text: The authors' ties to the company mean that the memory gain was probably exaggerated in the study.
options.explanation: Yazarlar çıkar ilişkilerini kendileri açıklar; bu, kazancın abartıldığını göstermez, yalnızca okurun bunu bilmesini sağlar.
